prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single, objectively “best” roofing company for every Dallas roof replacement — the right contractor depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial), roof type and material, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, budget, and schedule. I can help you find the best match. To start, tell me whether this is a home or commercial roof, the roof material you want (asphalt shingle, metal, tile, etc.), and whether insurance is involved.

Meanwhile, here’s a practical checklist and process to find a top-quality Dallas roofer, plus red flags to avoid.

Checklist for choosing a roofer
- Get 3 written estimates that itemize materials, labor, permits, and cleanup.  
- Verify insurance: ask for a certificate of insurance showing general liability and workers’ comp and confirm it’s current.  
- Check credentials: look for manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred), and membership in industry associations.  
- Local experience: prefer companies with a solid track record in the Dallas area and local references.  
- References and portfolio: ask for recent project photos and 3 local references you can call.  
- Written contract: include project scope, exact materials/brands, start and completion dates, payment schedule, cleanup, and warranty details.  
- Warranties: confirm manufacturer shingle warranty and installer workmanship warranty in writing.  
- Permits and inspections: ensure the contractor will obtain required permits and coordinate final inspections.  
- Payment terms: avoid large upfront payments; a typical schedule is small deposit, progress payments, and final payment upon completion and lien release.  
- Clean-up and property protection: confirm how they’ll protect landscaping and clean up nails and debris.

Red flags to avoid
- No written estimate or contract.  
- Requests for full payment upfront or pressure to sign immediately.  
- No proof of insurance or license/registration (ask for certificate).  
- Vague warranty promises, or “lifetime” claims without written backing.  
- Extremely low bids that seem too good to be true.  
- Lack of local references or poor online reviews that point to repeated problems.

How I can help right now
- I can search current Dallas-area roofers and give you a short list of well-reviewed, certified contractors.  
- I can draft questions to ask when you call for estimates, or a comparison sheet to evaluate proposals.  
- If you already have 1–2 estimates, I can review them and point out differences and concerns.

Which of those would you like me to do? If you want a shortlist, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial.
